title: Rigveda 10.86: Indra, Indrani and Vrishakapi
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.86: Indra, Indrani and Vrishakapi: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.86 is a hymn of 23 verses addressed to song of Vrisakapi. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 56r-58r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.

Gaps: verses 10.86.16, 10.86.17 were left untranslated by Griffith and are not shown.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
This manuscript inserts khila verses (supplementary hymns outside Aufrecht's text) at some hymn ends; they are noted in the section notes and not reproduced.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.86.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 4, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 56r
translation.original_text:
1vi hi soto̱r asṛ̍kṣata̱ nendra̍ṁ de̱vam a̍maṁsata | yatrāma̍dad vṛ̱ṣāka̍pir a̱ryaḥ pu̱ṣṭeṣu̱ matsa̍khā̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
2parā̱ hī̍ndra̱ dhāva̍si vṛ̱ṣāka̍pe̱r ati̱ vyathi̍ḥ | no aha̱ pra vi̍ndasy a̱nyatra̱ soma̍pītaye̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
translation.text:
1MEN have abstained from pouring juice they count not Indra as a God. Where at the votary's store my friend Vr̥ishâkapi hath drunk his fill. Supreme is Indra over all.
2Thou, Indra, heedless passest by the ill Vr̥ishâkapi hath wrought; Yet nowhere else thou findest place wherein to drink the Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 56r (numbered 55r by the scribe) (OPenn image 55, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.86.1 ‹vi hi sotor asṛkṣata›. Lines 1-3 carry khila verses appended to 10.85 (begun on 55v line 2, after 10.85.47) and the colophon of adhyaya 59 (ity ekonaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ); 10.86.1 begins in line 4. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 56v (numbered 55v by the scribe), begins in RV 10.86.3 ‹-harito mṛgaḥ›. Verses 10.86.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.86.3-7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 4, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 56v
translation.original_text:
3kim a̱yaṁ tvāṁ vṛ̱ṣāka̍piś ca̱kāra̱ hari̍to mṛ̱gaḥ | yasmā̍ ira̱syasīd u̱ nv a1̱̍ryo vā̍ puṣṭi̱mad vasu̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
4yam i̱maṁ tvaṁ vṛ̱ṣāka̍pim pri̱yam i̍ndrābhi̱rakṣa̍si | śvā nv a̍sya jambhiṣa̱d api̱ karṇe̍ varāha̱yur viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
5pri̱yā ta̱ṣṭāni̍ me ka̱pir vya̍ktā̱ vy a̍dūduṣat | śiro̱ nv a̍sya rāviṣa̱ṁ na su̱gaṁ du̱ṣkṛte̍ bhuva̱ṁ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
6na mat strī su̍bha̱satta̍rā̱ na su̱yāśu̍tarā bhuvat | na mat prati̍cyavīyasī̱ na sakthy udya̍mīyasī̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
7u̱ve a̍mba sulābhike̱ yathe̍vā̱ṅga bha̍vi̱ṣyati̍ | bha̱san me̍ amba̱ sakthi̍ me̱ śiro̍ me̱ vī̍va hṛṣyati̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
translation.text:
3What hath he done to injure thee, this tawny beast Vr̥ishâkapi, With whom thou art so angry now? What is the votary's foodful store? Supreme is Indra over all.
4Soon may the hound who hunts the boar seize him and bite him in the ear, O Indra, that Vr̥ishâkapi whom thou protectest as a friend, Supreme is Indra over all.
5Kapi hath marred the beauteous things, all deftly wrought, that were my joy. In pieces will I rend his head; the sinner's portion shall be woe. Supreme is Indra over all.
6No Dame hath ampler charms than I, or greater wealth of love's delights. None with more ardour offers all her beauty to her lord's embrace. Supreme is Indra over all.
7Mother whose love is quickly wibn, I say what verily will be. My,breast, O Mother, and my head and both my hips seem quivering. Supreme is Indra over all.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.86.8-13 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 4, varga 2); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 57r
translation.original_text:
8kiṁ su̍bāho svaṅgure̱ pṛthu̍ṣṭo̱ pṛthu̍jāghane | kiṁ śū̍rapatni na̱s tvam a̱bhy a̍mīṣi vṛ̱ṣāka̍pi̱ṁ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
9a̱vīrā̍m iva̱ mām a̱yaṁ śa̱rāru̍r a̱bhi ma̍nyate | u̱tāham a̍smi vī̱riṇīndra̍patnī ma̱rutsa̍khā̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
10sa̱ṁho̱traṁ sma̍ pu̱rā nārī̱ sama̍na̱ṁ vāva̍ gacchati | ve̱dhā ṛ̱tasya̍ vī̱riṇīndra̍patnī mahīyate̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
11i̱ndrā̱ṇīm ā̱su nāri̍ṣu su̱bhagā̍m a̱ham a̍śravam | na̱hy a̍syā apa̱raṁ ca̱na ja̱rasā̱ mara̍te̱ pati̱r viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
12nāham i̍ndrāṇi rāraṇa̱ sakhyu̍r vṛ̱ṣāka̍per ṛ̱te | yasye̱dam apya̍ṁ ha̱viḥ pri̱yaṁ de̱veṣu̱ gaccha̍ti̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
13vṛṣā̍kapāyi̱ reva̍ti̱ supu̍tra̱ ād u̱ susnu̍ṣe | ghasa̍t ta̱ indra̍ u̱kṣaṇa̍ḥ pri̱yaṁ kā̍citka̱raṁ ha̱vir viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
translation.text:
8Dame with the lovely hands and arms, with broad hair-plaits add ample hips, Why, O thou Hero's wife, art thou angry with our Vr̥ishâkapi? Supreme is Indra over all.
9This noxious creature looks on me as one bereft of hero's love, Yet Heroes for my sons have I, the Maruts' Friend and Indra's Queen. Supreme is Indra over all.
10From olden time the matron goes to feast and general sacrifice. Mother of Heroes, Indra's Queen, the rite's ordainer is extolled. Supreme is Indra over all.
11So have I heard Indrâṇî called most fortunate among these Dames, For never shall her Consort die in future time through length of days. Supreme is Indra overall.
12Never, Indrâṇî, have I joyed without my friend Vr̥ishâkapi, Whose welcome offering here, made pure with water, goeth to the Gods. Supreme is Indra over all.
13Wealthy Vrsakapayi, blest with sons and consorts of thy sons, Indra will eat thy bulls, thy dear oblation that effecteth much. Supreme is Indra over all.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.86.14-18 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 4, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 57v
translation.original_text:
14u̱kṣṇo hi me̱ pañca̍daśa sā̱kam paca̍nti viṁśa̱tim | u̱tāham a̍dmi̱ pīva̱ id u̱bhā ku̱kṣī pṛ̍ṇanti me̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
15vṛ̱ṣa̱bho na ti̱gmaśṛ̍ṅgo̱ 'ntar yū̱theṣu̱ roru̍vat | ma̱nthas ta̍ indra̱ śaṁ hṛ̱de yaṁ te̍ su̱noti̍ bhāva̱yur viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
18a̱yam i̍ndra vṛ̱ṣāka̍pi̱ḥ para̍svantaṁ ha̱taṁ vi̍dat | a̱siṁ sū̱nāṁ nava̍ṁ ca̱rum ād edha̱syāna̱ āci̍ta̱ṁ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
translation.text:
14Fifteen in number, then, for me a score of bullocks they prepare, And I devour the fat thereof: they fill my belly full with food. Supreme is Indra over all.
15Like as a bull with pointed horn, loud bellowing amid the herds, Sweet to thine heart, O Indra, is the brew which she who tends thee pours. Supreme is Indra over all.
18O Indra this Vr̥ishâkapi hath found a slain wild animal, Dresser, and new-made pan, and knife, and wagon with a load of wood. Supreme is Indra over all.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.86.19-23 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 4, varga 4); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 58r
translation.original_text:
19a̱yam e̍mi vi̱cāka̍śad vici̱nvan dāsa̱m ārya̍m | pibā̍mi pāka̱sutva̍no̱ 'bhi dhīra̍m acākaśa̱ṁ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
20dhanva̍ ca̱ yat kṛ̱ntatra̍ṁ ca̱ kati̍ svi̱t tā vi yoja̍nā | nedī̍yaso vṛṣāka̱pe 'sta̱m ehi̍ gṛ̱hām̐ upa̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
21puna̱r ehi̍ vṛṣākape suvi̱tā ka̍lpayāvahai | ya e̱ṣa sva̍pna̱naṁśa̱no 'sta̱m eṣi̍ pa̱thā puna̱r viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
22yad uda̍ñco vṛṣākape gṛ̱ham i̱ndrāja̍gantana | kva1̱̍ sya pu̍lva̱gho mṛ̱gaḥ kam a̍gañ jana̱yopa̍no̱ viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
23parśu̍r ha̱ nāma̍ māna̱vī sā̱kaṁ sa̍sūva viṁśa̱tim | bha̱dram bha̍la̱ tyasyā̍ abhū̱d yasyā̍ u̱dara̱m āma̍ya̱d viśva̍smā̱d indra̱ utta̍raḥ ||
translation.text:
19Distinguishing the Dâsa and the Ârya, viewing all, I go. I look upon the wise, and drink the simple votary's Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.
20The desert plains and steep descents, how many leagues in length they spread! Go to the nearest houses, go unto thine home, Vr̥ishâkapi. Supreme is Indra over all.
21Turn thee again Vr̥ishâkapi: we twain will bring thee happiness. Thou goest homeward on thy way along this path which leads to sleep. Supreme is Indra over all.
22When, Indra and Vr̥ishâkapi, ye travelled upward to your home, Where was that noisome beast, to whom went it, the beast that troubles man? Supreme is Indra over all.
23Daughter of Manu, Parṣu bare a score of children at a birth. Her portion verily was bliss although her burthen caused her grief.
